# RETRO: omacom/omarchy#12394 (team 4)

## What worked
- Source-only review resolved every material question; no hardware or desktop slot needed.
- A single neutral follow-up to Sol both confirmed a single-sourced finding (Copilot 0030) and made Sol correct its own packaged-version claim.

## Process deviations (coordinator)
1. WORKFLOW.md was read in seven parallel 50-line Read calls in one response, exceeding the 60-line aggregate-per-response bound that includes parallel calls. Later reads were sequential.
2. `pi_job.py wait` stdout (and `status`) include `latest_text`, which exposed a one-line Sol headline before the Opus final existed. Not disclosed to Opus. Suggest `pi_job.py wait/status` omit or gate `latest_text` until requested.
3. Used team 4's own prior brief (t4-12415) as a format template. A filename listing of the assignments directory also printed another team's brief path and line count; its content was not read.

## Reviewer-side
- The `omarchy-reviewer` subagent's write to `opus/REPORT.md` was refused by the harness ("Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files"). The subagent returned the report as text; the coordinator saved it with a provenance header. Its other files (`opus/RETRO.md`, `opus/ext/`) were written. Tooling issue: either allow the report write or have the brief say to return the report as text.
- Opus RETRO records its own deviations: one `ls -la` with owner/group names, one read over 50 lines, one host-side `python3 -B -c` JSON parse, one `cut -c1-400` safety cap (no truncation), a few fetches without separate receipts.

## Carry forward
- For udev/device-access PRs, include in the brief: install/upgrade delivery path and the consuming script's device-selection behaviour; both mattered here.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the new rule is valid udev syntax on current systemd. `ATTRS{idProduct}=="0012|0013|0014|0018|0019"` is five exact alternatives matched on the module's USB device, and `SUBSYSTEM=="hidraw"` limits the grant to hidraw nodes, so `/dev/input/eventN` gets no new ACL (the PR's second test-plan item holds). The five IDs are the Framework firmware PIDs for the ANSI keyboard, RGB macropad, numpad, ISO keyboard and JIS keyboard. Nothing that works on the base rule regresses.

Four points limit what the change delivers: existing installs never receive it, the hidraw-only scope still exposes keyboard input reports, theme syncing still does not reach the added modules, and one RGB keyboard PID is missing.

### Existing installs keep the old rule

`install/hardware/framework/qmk-hid.sh` copies the rule to `/etc/udev/rules.d/50-framework16-qmk-hid.rules` only when that file does not exist, and no migration touches it:

```bash
if [[ ! -f /etc/udev/rules.d/50-framework16-qmk-hid.rules ]]; then
  sudo cp -f "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/udev/framework16-qmk-hid.rules" /etc/udev/rules.d/50-framework16-qmk-hid.rules
fi
```

**Impact:** every Framework 16 that was already installed keeps the `0012`-only file after updating, and rerunning the hardware installer skips the copy. Only fresh installs get the new IDs.

**Suggested change:** add a migration (per `docs/file-layout.md`) that replaces the file only when its content is exactly the old shipped line, so administrator edits are left alone, then reloads udev and re-triggers hidraw devices or tells the user a reboot or module re-seat is needed.

### `SUBSYSTEM=="hidraw"` still grants access to keystroke reports

The description says the hidraw-only rule matches Framework's coverage "without the exposure" of raw keystroke capture. The rule does keep `input` devices untouched, but the Linux HID stack creates a hidraw node for **every** HID interface of the module, and the rule's VID/PID match sits on their shared USB parent:

```text
usb_device 32ac:0012   <- ATTRS{idVendor}/ATTRS{idProduct} match here
├─ interface 00 (keyboard)  ─ hidraw  <- matched, uaccess ACL; carries key input reports
│                           └ input/eventN  (not matched)
├─ interface 01 (VIA raw HID) ─ hidraw  <- matched; the only one qmk_hid uses
└─ shared / console interfaces ─ hidraw <- matched
```

The kernel copies every input report to every open hidraw reader, so any process of the active seat user can read keystrokes from the keyboard interface's hidraw node.

**Impact:** this was already true for `0012` on the base rule. The PR extends it to the ISO and JIS keyboards, numpad and macropad, and the description presents the opposite.

**Suggested change:** at minimum, correct the security wording in the description. Optional approach: limit the grant to interface `01`, which QMK reserves for raw HID. A single line cannot do this, because `bInterfaceNumber` lives on the USB interface and all `ATTRS` keys in one rule must match the same parent. A two-line form (first line matches VID/PID and sets a marker `ENV`, second requires the marker plus `ATTRS{bInterfaceNumber}=="01"`) should work but is untested and needs hardware validation. VIA access on interface 1 still allows reading the key-matrix state, so this narrows rather than removes key visibility.

### Theme syncing still does not reach the added modules

The description gives missing udev coverage as the reason RGB theme syncing does not reach the macropad and other modules. The rule is necessary but not sufficient. Expected behaviour from source review, not executed on a device:

| Modules attached | `omarchy-theme-set-keyboard-f16` expected result, base | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| ANSI `0012` only | colour applied | unchanged |
| ISO `0018` or JIS `0019` only | device not opened (permission) | opened, but no RGB matrix: colour does not change |
| keyboard + macropad `0013` or numpad `0014` | `qmk_hid`: "More than 1 device found. Select a specific device with --vid and --pid" | same refusal |

`qmk_hid` (v0.1.13 as packaged for Omarchy, and v0.1.11) enumerates devices from sysfs without opening them, so the multi-device refusal happens regardless of permissions. The script's five `qmk_hid via ...` calls pass no `--vid`/`--pid`. The numpad, ISO and JIS firmware is built with white backlight only (`RGB_MATRIX_ENABLE` is set only for ANSI, ANSI Copilot and the macropad), and `qmk_hid`'s RGB commands target the RGB matrix channel. This is a pre-existing script limitation, not a regression.

**Impact:** the added IDs enable manual `qmk_hid` / VIA use, but Omarchy's theme colour still reaches none of the added modules.

**Suggested change:** either narrow the description to unprivileged `qmk_hid` / VIA access, or also update the theme script to address each RGB-capable module explicitly, for example `qmk_hid --vid 32ac --pid <id> via ...` for `0012`, `0013` and `0030`.

### ANSI Copilot keyboard (`0030`) is missing

Framework's QMK firmware (release v0.3.1 and the newest `fl16` branch) builds six Laptop 16 variants, and fwupd's `framework-qmk` quirk lists the same six. The sixth is `keyboards/framework/copilot`, "Laptop 16 Keyboard Module - ANSI Copilot", PID `0x0030`, with the same RGB matrix as ANSI. The community guide the PR follows also omits it.

**Impact:** on a laptop whose only QMK module is the Copilot keyboard, `qmk_hid` finds one device but cannot open it, and the theme script hides the error, so theme syncing fails silently. It is the one unlisted module where the rule alone would make theme syncing work.

**Suggested change:** add `0030` to the alternation, `ATTRS{idProduct}=="0012|0013|0014|0018|0019|0030"`.

**Test scope:** source review of head `7b3b6bf` (unchanged relative to the current `quattro` tip for the rule, installer and theme script), plus the source of systemd-udev 262, Linux HID/hidraw, `qmk_hid` v0.1.11 and v0.1.13, Framework's QMK firmware and fwupd's quirk file. Nothing was executed: no udev rule was installed or triggered, and no Framework 16 hardware was available, so neither test-plan item and none of the conclusions above were checked on a device. The interface-01 rule sketch is untested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with a targeted follow-up to confirm the product-ID list and packaged `qmk_hid` version, and an Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
